paras: The Alexandria street assault of September 1903 was an attempted attack by two white men on an unnamed Black man on a street in Alexandria on the evening of Monday, 21 September 1903. One of the men struck at him, but he escaped, and no arrests were made. The incident is known only from a short item in the local news column of the Alexandria Gazette.

According to the Gazette, two white men who, "for some cause," wanted to assault "a colored man" drew the attention of "numbers of passersby" on the evening before its Tuesday, 22 September issue. One of the two struck at the man, who got away from his assailants. The item does not name the victim or the attackers, give the street, or say whether the blow landed or caused any injury.
The Gazette stated that no arrests were made, and no later report of the incident was found in either the white or the Black press.

The Alexandria Gazette ran the report without a headline in its "Local Brevities" column of 22 September 1903, between a notice of the opening of the circuit court and an invitation to a Confederate veterans' camp. The paragraph called the victim "a colored man" and then "the darkey," and it offered no motive beyond "some cause." No other white paper and no Black paper in the collections searched carried the story.

bases: Two white men attempted a street assault on a colored man, one striking at him before he escaped (A1); no larger crowd took part, so this is an attempted assault by two individuals rather than a mob.
A single brief local item in the Alexandria Gazette is the only report found in either press (A1).

accounts.label: Local news column
accounts.gist: Two white men, for an unstated cause, tried to assault a colored man before numerous passersby; one struck at him, he escaped, and no arrests were made.

framing.detail: A brief, unheadlined item in 'Local Brevities' between court and social notices, giving no motive and using 'the darkey' for the victim.

record_check.record: ...tried to assault a colored man on the street Sunday evening...
record_check.dossier: Monday evening: the item ran in the Tuesday, 22 September issue and says 'yesterday evening'; event_date 1903-09-21 is right but 'Sunday' is wrong.
Two individual white men; no mob or crowd took part (passersby only watched).
Attempted assault: one man struck at the victim, who escaped; no beating or injury is reported.
